whatIs.title: What is a Performance Bonus?
whatIs.description: A performance bonus is additional compensation paid beyond base salary, determined by company profitability or individual performance. In Korean companies, bonuses come in various forms including PS (Profit Sharing), PI (Productivity Incentive), management performance bonuses, and individual incentives. PS distributes a portion of company profits to employees, primarily at large corporations like Samsung and Hyundai, with amounts ranging from 0% to several hundred percent of monthly base pay. PI is awarded based on department or team-level target achievement. Under Korean tax law, bonuses are classified as earned income, subject to progressive income tax (6-45%) and local income tax (10% of income tax); employment insurance is deducted in the payment month, health and long-term care insurance are charged at the following April settlement, and no extra National Pension is withheld in the bonus month. When a bonus is added, total annual income increases, potentially pushing the taxpayer into a higher tax bracket with a higher marginal rate, resulting in a greater perceived tax burden. This calculator applies the 2026 tax rates and social insurance contribution rates to automatically compute deductions and take-home amounts from your pre-tax salary and bonus inputs. The ratio simulation feature lets you compare scenarios from 50% to 500% of monthly pay at a glance, while the tax structure analysis visually shows how tax brackets and additional tax burdens change with and without the bonus.

tips.title: Tax-Saving Tips for Bonuses
items: Contribute your bonus to an IRP (Individual Retirement Pension) for up to 9M KRW tax credit
Combined with pension savings, up to 9M KRW annual tax credit (16.5% if salary ≤55M KRW)
Splitting a bonus within the same year leaves annual tax unchanged; only a different tax year can lower the marginal rate
Maximize non-taxable benefits like meal allowances (200K KRW/month)
Don't miss additional deductions at year-end (medical, education, donations, etc.)

items.q: Are social insurance contributions applied to bonuses?
items.a: In the bonus month only employment insurance (0.9%) and income tax are withheld. National pension uses a fixed monthly base, and health insurance on the bonus is charged at next April's settlement. The pension monthly income cap is 6.59M KRW from Jul 2026 to Jun 2027 (6.37M in Jan-Jun 2026).

items.q: Why does the tax rate on bonuses seem higher than regular salary?
items.a: The bonus itself isn't taxed at a higher rate. Rather, adding the bonus increases your total annual income, potentially pushing you into a higher progressive tax bracket (6-45% in Korea).

items.q: How much can I save by putting my bonus into a retirement pension?
items.a: An IRP, combined with pension savings, earns a tax credit on up to 9M KRW a year (the contribution limit is 18M KRW combined). The credit is 16.5% for salary up to 55M KRW and 13.2% above, so a 9M KRW contribution returns up to 1.485M KRW.

items.q: Why do withholding taxes differ from actual taxes?
items.a: Withholding uses simplified tax tables for monthly deductions. Year-end settlement reconciles with actual income and deductions. Even if a large amount is withheld from a bonus month, you may get a refund.

items.q: What's the difference between a bonus and performance pay?
items.a: A regular bonus splits the annual salary into extra payments on specific months (total unchanged). Performance pay is additional income beyond the annual salary. Tax calculation methods are the same.

items.q: Does splitting bonus payments across months reduce taxes?
items.a: Splitting bonus payments across months may lower the withholding rate per month, but since total annual income remains the same, the final tax amount at year-end settlement is identical. However, it can help with cash flow management.

items.q: Are bonuses received after resignation still taxed?
items.a: Yes. A bonus paid after you leave is still earned income (not retirement income), so income tax (plus local income tax) is withheld before payment. No separate National Pension contribution is taken from it; employment and health insurance follow the employer's annual wage-total report and settlement.
